inputs.userGoal: Migrate the complete hybridcloudworks.com workload from Personal-Site_HCW into this repository using a cost-conscious, five-pillar Azure architecture, Azure Verified Modules, Terraform, and GitHub-first delivery.
subGoals: Cost-conscious production foundation with a USD 150 monthly budget ceiling and one production workload state.
Security-first admin plane using Microsoft Entra ID, managed identities, least privilege, and no static Azure credentials.
Static-first public delivery with measurable reliability and a staged Firebase-to-Azure rollback boundary.

reasoning.whyChosen: Creates one production workload, cost, policy, and access boundary.
reasoning.tradeoffs: A single workload group is simpler and cheaper to operate, but service-level lifecycle separation is handled through Terraform modules and identities instead of resource groups.

overallReasoning.summary: The target is a static-first Azure workload with an anonymous public plane, Entra-protected admin plane, isolated serverless execution boundaries, identity-based data access, durable asynchronous workflows, centralized observability, and GitHub-governed delivery. The design preserves the complete source workload through migration domains rather than treating the incomplete existing Azure attempt as authoritative.
overallReasoning.tradeoffs: The USD 150 ceiling intentionally defers Azure Front Door, Azure Firewall, NAT Gateway, API Management, multiregion data, always-ready compute, and Private Link for Function host storage and Azure OpenAI. Cloudflare remains the edge. Cosmos DB Serverless accepts a regional-outage limitation. Selective private endpoints protect Cosmos, content Blob/Queue Storage, and Key Vault because the Flex integration subnet cannot use the originally proposed service-endpoint pattern. Isolated Function host storage remains public at the service endpoint but contains only platform state and uses identity-first access. Azure OpenAI is feature-gated until capacity and budget are confirmed. Only one production workload state is planned; bootstrap identity and state trust remain a separate administrative lifecycle boundary.

plan.validation: The draft topology has coherent compute, storage, identity, networking, observability, and delivery dependencies. Region-specific SKU availability, Azure OpenAI capacity, Cosmos partition keys, exact AVM module versions, and monthly list-price calculations must be verified before IaC generation.
architecturePrinciples: Static first: public browsing does not depend on live database reads or AI availability.
Identity first: managed identity and Entra RBAC replace service keys wherever supported.
Least privilege by execution boundary: API, background work, and labs do not share broad identities.
Async side effects: external publishing and notifications are retry-safe, idempotent, observable, and poison-queue protected.
Cost is a design constraint: serverless capacity, bounded telemetry, lifecycle policies, quotas, tags, and budgets are code.
One reviewed artifact moves forward: GitHub plan, approval, apply, deployment, and rollback evidence remain connected.
Migration is reversible until acceptance gates pass; Firebase decommissioning is a separate approval.
